messages:
anya: FYI I converted the HF checkpoint for client-x and smoke tests surfaced a pile of silent config mismatches when Redwood loader tried to bring it up. posting quick notes and logs.
matt: ugh, list pls — what broke?
anya: short: rope_scaling either missing or set to null, sliding_window absent (defaults caused weird kv-cache behavior), num_key_value_heads != num_attention_heads -> KV shape mismatch at init, and max_position_embeddings was too low for the tokenizer leading to truncation.
sara: did this happen before quantization or after?
anya: both. conversion alone fails on init if kv heads mismatch. after we force-convert and run int8 quant, evals show quality regression — looks like truncation + kv misalign makes predictions worse.
anya: snippet from converted config.json we saw:
```
"rope_scaling": null,
"sliding_window": 0,
"num_key_value_heads": 8,
"num_attention_heads": 16,
"max_position_embeddings": 2048
```
but the tokenizer and the dataset use long-context templates (up to ~3500 tokens).
matt: so RW runtime expects explicit rope_scaling and sliding_window semantics. Anything in hf model card?
anya: model card had vague note about 'rope v2', but HF conversion path set rope_scaling to null. sliding_window absent -> Redwood runtime treated as 0 and didn't rotate/roll KV properly leading to cache blowups under continuous-chat.
geoff: that explains the intermittent segfaults we saw in dedicated-mode yesterday.
sara: numbers from the eval run: baseline hosted model -> rouge-l 32.7. converted+int8 -> rouge-l 31.1 (~4.8% drop). turning quant off but keeping converted config -> rouge-l 31.8. turning quant back on but fixing max_position_embeddings -> 31.4. looks like both truncation and quant losses stack.
anya: minimal local workaround I used to repro-fix: update config to
```
"rope_scaling": {"type":"linear","factor":1.0},
"sliding_window": 256,
"num_key_value_heads": 16,
"max_position_embeddings": 4096
```
and ensure chat template maps special tokens (BOS/EOS) explicitly to tokenizer special ids. after that conversion -> rw runtime starts fine and evals recover ~within noise (+0.2–0.5).
matt: can converter detect/auto-fix these? we should avoid manual edits.
anya: opened issue #4332 with failing sample and proposed checks. PR incoming to rw-hf-convert to run a schema-check that: 1) verifies num_kv_heads divides/equals expectations, 2) warns if sliding_window is missing or 0 for chat templates, 3) checks rope_scaling presence or fallback rules, 4) compares max_position_embeddings to tokenizer longest sequence and warns.
infra-bot: rw-convert-check/195876 started -> status: failed -> logs: "KV cache init error: shape mismatch (expected 16, got 8)"
matt: nice. can you add an auto-suggest patch (dry-run) so users can accept a fix?
anya: yes planning a --apply-suggestions flag. also adding a unit test that runs conversion on a synthetic hf-config producing these exact mismatches so we don't regress.
sara: for the quant regressions we'll need a small bisect plan: quant kernels off -> on, per-layer ablation, and run our summary/regression evals. I'll take lead on that if you want.
anya: that would be great. I will push the hotfix for converter warnings and the patch-proposal today. sara: can you start the quant bisect once the patched model is converted?
sara: yup. ETA EOD tomorrow for first bisect pass.
matt: thanks. tagging @eng-runtime to be aware (they saw the segfaults). :thumbsup:
anya: FYI command I ran to repro: `rw-convert --model-dir ./hf-checkpoint --check-config --output ./rw-model` -> it now fails with a clear complaint. push PR shortly. :face_with_monocle:
